chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about a man who accuses another man of false testimony (qadhf), then the accuser pardons him, then he wants to flog him after his repentance. He said: He does not have that right after the pardon.
ai.seo_question: Does the qadhf punishment remain if the accuser pardons the accused and then changes his mind?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Samaanah clarifies that once the accuser pardons the accused of qadhf, the right to impose the hadd punishment is extinguished permanently, preventing re-imposition even after the accused's repentance. This ruling underscores the principle that the accuser's pardon is a definitive legal act that concludes the case, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the finality of judicial forgiveness in maintaining social harmony and preventing perpetual litigation.
